claims.claim: In a pre-registered study of 81 participants post-editing LLM drafts for personal writing tasks, the post-edited text still remained stylistically closer to LLM text than to the participants' own unassisted control text.
claims.source: Baumler, Bao, Nghiem, Yang, Carpuat and Daume III, University of Maryland, arXiv:2604.24444, April 2026
claims.quote: post-edited text still remains stylistically closer in style to LLM text
claims.routeHint: arXiv HTML at /html/2604.24444v1, direct curl with browser UA
claims.modelEra: drafts generated with GPT-o4-mini (OpenAI 2025); study conducted for the April 2026 preprint; register: personal occasional writing - wedding vows, apology letters, eulogies, condolence letters

claims.claim: The same study measured post-edited writing as significantly more stylistically homogeneous than unassisted writing, at p = .0002 with Hedges g = 1.42 and a 95% CI of [1.33, 1.51].
claims.source: Baumler et al., University of Maryland, arXiv:2604.24444, April 2026
claims.quote: post-edited writing is indeed more stylistically homogeneous than unassisted writing
claims.modelEra: GPT-o4-mini drafts, April 2026; register: personal occasional writing

claims.feature: other: which features survive human editing
claims.claim: The same study found participants' post-edited text significantly more stylistically similar to other participants' post-edited text than to their own control writing, showing that some features of the LLM stylistic fingerprint are consistently preserved after post-editing across different participants.
claims.source: Baumler et al., University of Maryland, arXiv:2604.24444, April 2026
claims.quote: are consistently preserved after post-editing across different participants
claims.modelEra: GPT-o4-mini drafts, April 2026; register: personal occasional writing

claims.feature: other: which features survive human editing
claims.claim: The study concludes that the human-like changes made during post-editing are meaningfully unique to individuals while the AI-like aspects that are not addressed during post-editing are meaningfully shared between participants.
claims.source: Baumler et al., University of Maryland, arXiv:2604.24444, April 2026
claims.quote: the AI-like aspects that are not addressed during post-editing
claims.modelEra: GPT-o4-mini drafts, April 2026; register: personal occasional writing

claims.claim: In the study's qualitative coding, some participant edits removed words or punctuation commonly associated with LLM-generated text, the examples given being em dashes and the word dive, while others added contractions.
claims.source: Baumler et al., University of Maryland, arXiv:2604.24444, April 2026
claims.quote: some edits removed words or punctuation commonly associated with LLM-generated text
claims.modelEra: GPT-o4-mini drafts, April 2026; register: personal occasional writing

claims.claim: The study reports that participants sometimes simplified sentence structure or removed flowery language, giving the example of cutting a phrase about a spirit whose generosity knew no bounds down to an amazing man.
claims.source: Baumler et al., University of Maryland, arXiv:2604.24444, April 2026
claims.quote: participants sometimes simplified sentence structure or removed flowery language
claims.modelEra: GPT-o4-mini drafts, April 2026; register: eulogy and condolence writing

claims.claim: The same study observed that other participants added cliched expressions during post-editing, which the authors take as evidence that such language was not uniformly viewed as uncharacteristic.
claims.source: Baumler et al., University of Maryland, arXiv:2604.24444, April 2026
claims.routeHint: arXiv HTML at /html/2604.24444v1; the quotation is cut before the accented character in 'clichéd' to keep it byte-exact
claims.modelEra: GPT-o4-mini drafts, April 2026; register: eulogy and condolence writing

claims.claim: The study found a gap between perceived stylistic authenticity and model-measured similarity: post-edited text was often perceived by its own editor as representative of their personal style despite remaining detectable LLM stylistic traces.
claims.source: Baumler et al., University of Maryland, arXiv:2604.24444, April 2026
claims.quote: despite remaining detectable LLM stylistic traces
claims.modelEra: GPT-o4-mini drafts, April 2026; register: personal occasional writing

claims.claim: The study's exploratory results suggest that adoption of the post-editing workflow is limited less by the effort of adjusting style than by a perceived lack of interesting or original content in the LLM-generated drafts.
claims.source: Baumler et al., University of Maryland, arXiv:2604.24444, April 2026
claims.quote: a perceived lack of interesting or original content in LLM-generated drafts
claims.page: Section 6.5, (Why) Do Participants Like to Post-Edit?
claims.confidence: medium - the authors label this result exploratory rather than pre-registered
claims.modelEra: GPT-o4-mini drafts, April 2026; register: personal occasional writing

claims.claim: Liang and colleagues measured LLM-assisted writing across four institutional registers from January 2022 to September 2024, on a corpus of 687,241 consumer complaints, 537,413 corporate press releases, 304.3 million job postings and 15,919 United Nations press releases.
claims.source: Weixin Liang, Yaohui Zhang, Mihai Codreanu, Jiayu Wang et al., Stanford and UW, arXiv:2502.09747, February 2025
claims.routeHint: arXiv HTML at /html/2502.09747v1, direct curl with browser UA
claims.modelEra: post-ChatGPT LLMs generally, corpus window January 2022 to September 2024; registers measured: consumer complaints, corporate press releases, job postings, UN press releases - institutional and official prose, not fiction

claims.claim: The study estimates that LLM-assisted content in United Nations press releases rose from 3.1% in Q1 2023 to 10.1% in Q3 2023 and reached 13.7% by Q3 2024.
claims.source: Liang, Zhang, Codreanu, Wang et al., arXiv:2502.09747, February 2025
claims.page: Section on LLM Adoption in United Nations Press Releases
claims.modelEra: post-ChatGPT LLMs, measured to Q3 2024; register: United Nations country-team press releases

claims.claim: The study estimates LLM-modified content in Newswire corporate press releases peaked at 24.3% in December 2023 and stabilised at 23.8% through September 2024.
claims.source: Liang, Zhang, Codreanu, Wang et al., arXiv:2502.09747, February 2025
claims.quote: peaking at 24.3% in December 2023 and stabilizing at 23.8%
claims.modelEra: post-ChatGPT LLMs, measured to September 2024; register: corporate press releases

claims.claim: The study reports the consumer-complaint estimate rising from a baseline algorithm false positive rate of 1.5% to 15.3% by August 2023, with only a modest increase to 17.7% through August 2024.
claims.source: Liang, Zhang, Codreanu, Wang et al., arXiv:2502.09747, February 2025
claims.quote: rose sharply from a baseline algorithm false positive rate of 1.5% to 15.3%
claims.modelEra: post-ChatGPT LLMs, measured to August 2024; register: financial consumer complaints

claims.claim: Liang and colleagues state explicitly that their study did not directly measure homogenization, and only point to prior academic research as a reason to expect similar effects in job postings.
claims.source: Liang, Zhang, Codreanu, Wang et al., arXiv:2502.09747, February 2025
claims.quote: our study did not directly measure homogenization
claims.modelEra: n/a - a statement of the study's own scope, February 2025; registers measured: institutional prose
